newsitem.title: MALAWI: Malawi court dismisses state appeal against Banda.
newsitem.headline: Malawi court dismisses state appeal against Banda.

text.p: Malawi's Supreme Court of Appeal on Thursday dismissed an appeal by the government to retry former president Kamuzu Banda on charges of plotting to murder four senior politicians of which he was acquitted.
In his ruling, Judge Lewis Chatsika said: "The whole appeal fails and is hereby dismissed in its entirety."

The government had lodged the appeal against a High Court ruling in 1995 which had found Banda not guilty on the charges of plotting to murder three cabinet ministers and a member of parliament in 1983.

Reacting to the ruling, Director of Public Prosecution Kamudoni Nyasulu conceded defeat. But he told reporters that the court action was a "cleansing for the nation" and equated it with the Truth and Reconciliation Commission in South Africa.
"It warns politicians that if they are not transparent something like this will happen to them," Nyasulu said.
Banda was prime minister when Malawi gained independence from Britain in 1964, became president in 1966 and proclaimed himself president for life in 1971, crushing dissent.
His grip on Malawi slipped when he lost the presidency to former protege Bakili Muluzi in the country's first democratic elections in 1994.
